We've seen several reports about Apple Vision Pro applications in medical settings. This week, Stryker announced the completion of the first surgical procedure performed using an innovative application on Vision Pro.

The procedure was a hip arthroscopy, using the SportSuite Vision application, which can bring "critical digital content into the surgeon's virtual space." This includes arthroscopic imaging, the HipCheck hip examination tool, HipMap, and CT scan images, among others.

Here is Stryker's description of the application:

SportSuite Vision brings critical digital content into the surgeon's visual space, allowing them to view arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, CT scan images, and other digital tools alongside physical objects in the operating room. During arthroscopic procedures, surgeons often rely on multiple screens in the operating room to access imaging and surgical data. By integrating multiple data sources into the surgeon's field of view, this technology can reduce reliance on traditional screens and support a smoother, more ergonomic surgical workflow.

SportSuite Vision received FDA De Novo authorization on July 17. Stryker stated that this application is the first FDA-approved application for use with Vision Pro during surgery.
